chapters.reason: The paper explicitly describes a model that iterates a recurrent block to unroll to arbitrary depth at test-time, which is an architectural modification for recurrence, aligning with the 'explicit structural modifications' and 'adaptive computation time' key phrases. It contrasts with training-induced recurrence.

The work focuses on scaling test-time compute by increasing depth (recurrent iterations), treating depth as a computational resource that enhances reasoning performance, which directly relates to the concept of layer depth as a primary bottleneck for latent reasoning capacity.

The model's recurrent block iteration at test-time to achieve unbounded depth and improve reasoning resembles the 'adaptive self-iterations' and 'convergence halting' described for implicit fixed-point RNNs, though it is not explicitly framed as reaching a fixed-point equilibrium.
